agent.problem: Card 5 already asks whose lives the righteousness of Noah, Daniel and Job can deliver in Ezekiel 14:14. Card 10 asks that same repeated line again for Ezekiel 14:20, rather than asking about it only at its first appearance.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

human.problem: The card says the Daniel of Ezekiel 14:14 is the Daniel taken from Judah to Babylon (Daniel 1:1-6). Ezekiel 14 doesn't say this, and whether the two are the same man is debated. The papa-dorin.md "New people" rule says to say who someone is. The "Leave open what the text leaves open" and "Connecting passages" rules point toward not linking passages the text doesn't link. No rule settles this case.
human.question: When the passage itself doesn't identify a person, as with the Daniel of Ezekiel 14:14, should Papa Dorin give the traditional identification with a cross-reference, or only name him as the text does?

human.problem: The card says Ezekiel's Daniel is the Daniel 'taken from Judah to Babylon (Daniel 1:1-6).' Ezekiel 14:14 gives only the name. Some interpreters read this Daniel as someone other than the Daniel of the book of Daniel. The docs allow 'facts from outside the passage' about 'who a new person is.' They don't say what to do when who the person is depends on interpretation.
human.question: Should Papa Dorin say this is the Daniel of the book of Daniel, or only give the name as Ezekiel 14:14 does?
